title: Rewrite 6.4 with hundredths
text: $$2.18$$ has hundredths, so rewrite $$6.4$$ as $$6.40$$ before you subtract. A common mistake is to treat 6.4 as 6.04, or to subtract 18 from 4 and ignore the ones. In hundredths, $$6.40$$ is 640 hundredths and $$2.18$$ is 218 hundredths. What is $$640 - 218$$?

title: Turn hundredths back into a decimal
text: 422 hundredths means 4 ones and 22 hundredths, because 100 hundredths make 1. What decimal equals 422 hundredths?

title: Worked solution
text: $$6.40 - 2.18 = 4.22$$. Check: $$4.22 + 2.18 = 6.40$$. Common mistake: answering $$4.38$$ by subtracting 4 minus 18 incorrectly and borrowing the wrong place. General rule: give both numbers the same number of decimal places, then subtract place by place, borrowing from the place to the left when you need to.
